# PeachPrep RE

> Free Georgia real estate exam prep — a free practice quiz and the PeachPrep RE iOS app with 1,900+ GA-specific practice questions, 400+ flashcards, and full-length 152-question PSI-style timed practice exams.

Exam-format facts on these pages (152 questions = 100 national + 52 Georgia supplement, both portions scored separately at 75%, 4-hour limit, administered by PSI) are verified against the official PSI/GREC candidate information bulletin.

## Study guides & exam facts

- [Georgia Real Estate Exam Study Plan: 30 Days, 2 Weeks, or 48 Hours](https://peachprepre.com/study-plan.html): Pick the study plan that matches your exam date — a 30-day build, a 21-day or 14-day review, a one-week triage, or a 48-hour final review. Each plan says what to study, what to skip, and when to take full-length timed practice exams. Includes advice for studying with a full-time job, a toddler at home, ADHD, or pregnancy. Built around the real 152-question, 4-hour Georgia PSI salesperson exam (100 national + 52 state, 75% required on both portions).
- [How Much Does Real Estate School Cost in Georgia? (And How Long It Really Takes)](https://peachprepre.com/school.html): Expect $205–$520 for the single required 75-hour GREC-approved salesperson pre-license course — every approved school teaches the same curriculum; typical part-time pace is 4–8 weeks. Georgia's quirk: after the course everything moves in days (same-day GCIC report, instant PSI results, license issued at the test center — allow 24 hours). Time the GCIC report for the final course week (must be under 60 days old when used). Retakes cost the full $175. Includes a 30% Aceable Agent referral discount (disclosed).
- [Georgia Real Estate Exam Vocabulary: 50 Terms You Need to Know](https://peachprepre.com/vocab.html): The 50 most-tested Georgia real estate exam terms — from BRRETA, brokerage engagements, and designated agency to security deeds, the intangible recording tax, and Georgia's power-of-sale foreclosure — with plain-English, exam-focused definitions organized by topic. Includes the Georgia-only concepts national prep material skips.
- [Free Georgia Real Estate Practice Questions](https://peachprepre.com/practice-questions.html): 20 free Georgia real estate exam practice questions with answers and explanations — covering license law, agency, contracts, finance, valuation, and more. National + state portions, no email required.
- [How Many Questions Is the Georgia Real Estate Exam? Format, Time Limit & Passing Score](https://peachprepre.com/exam-facts.html): The Georgia salesperson exam is 152 questions (100 national + 52 Georgia supplement, plus 1–10 unscored experimental items) in one 4-hour sitting — you need 75% on each portion, scored separately with no averaging. Exam fee is $175 per attempt as of July 2026 (many sites still quote the old fee); retakes can be scheduled as soon as two days after a fail. Georgia issues your license at the PSI test center — allow 24 hours after passing, $170 license fee covers the first four years, and you must apply within 12 months of passing. Per the official PSI Georgia Candidate Information Bulletin (July 2026) and the Georgia Real Estate Commission.
- [What to Bring to the Georgia Real Estate Exam (And What Gets You Turned Away)](https://peachprepre.com/exam-day.html): Georgia's exam-day packing list is ONE valid, unexpired government-issued photo ID bearing your signature, matching the name you scheduled under (driver's license, state ID, US or foreign passport, US military ID, or alien registration card) — no proper ID means an invalid registration and a forfeited exam fee. Handheld calculators are PROHIBITED; PSI provides an on-screen calculator plus scratch paper and a pencil. Also banned per PSI's bulletin: all electronics (phones, smart watches, earbuds), reference materials, non-religious hats, bulky or loose outerwear (open sweaters, cardigans, jackets), food, drinks, gum, purses, wallets, and 'good luck items.' Arrive 30 minutes early — arriving after start time forfeits the $175 fee, and cancellations need 2 days' notice. No guests may wait anywhere on the property. The exam: a 15-minute tutorial that doesn't count against time, then 152 scored questions in 4 hours (75% on each portion, scored separately); you can revisit and change answers until time runs out. Your score appears on screen immediately and a score report is emailed; a failed report includes a diagnostic breakdown, and retakes can be scheduled as soon as two days later. Per PSI's official Georgia Candidate Information Bulletin.
- [Georgia Real Estate Exam Math: The Formulas That Actually Show Up](https://peachprepre.com/math.html): Yes, there is math on the Georgia salesperson exam — Real Estate Calculations is 7% of the 100-question national portion (per PSI's content outline), and the Georgia supplement's Finance & Closing block (15 of 52 questions) adds state-specific math. Georgia-only formulas: transfer tax = $1.00 for the first $1,000 of consideration plus $0.10 per additional $100 (seller customarily pays; works out to $1 per $1,000); intangible recording tax = $1.50 per $500 of a long-term note's face amount (borrower pays); property is assessed at 40% of fair market value (set by Georgia law) before applying millage, with a $2,000 standard homestead exemption off assessed value. Also covered: commissions, percent profit, prorations (Georgia taxes paid in arrears), LTV, simple interest, IRV/cap rates, and 1 acre = 43,560 sq ft. PSI provides an on-screen calculator at the test center.
- [Georgia Real Estate License Reciprocity: Every State Qualifies (One Exception)](https://peachprepre.com/reciprocity.html): Georgia offers licensing by reciprocity to licensees from ALL states (per GREC): if you earned your license by passing another state's exam and it is currently in good standing, you can obtain the equivalent Georgia license with no exam and no 75-hour course — just the Real Estate Reciprocal Application. The one exception: licensed Florida residents must pass a supplemental exam, which is the 52-question Georgia portion of the state exam (75% to pass, scheduled through PSI). Georgia licenses also travel well — Florida grants Georgia licensees mutual recognition via a 40-question Florida law exam.
- [How Long Does It Take to Get a Georgia Real Estate License?](https://peachprepre.com/how-long.html): Most people take 2–4 months, dominated by the 75-hour pre-license course (4–8 weeks part-time). Then a same-day GCIC report and the PSI exam with instant results — PSI can issue your license at the test center itself (they say to allow 24 hours). Full step-by-step timeline.
- [I Failed the Georgia Real Estate Exam — What Now?](https://peachprepre.com/fail.html): Exactly how the Georgia retake works — the $175 retake fee (no portion discount), the days-not-weeks turnaround, why you only retake the portion you failed, Georgia's veteran preference points, and how to study differently for the next attempt.
- [How Much Does It Cost to Get a Georgia Real Estate License? (2026 Fee Breakdown)](https://peachprepre.com/cost.html): Expect $560–$890 all-in: $205–$520 for the required 75-hour pre-license course, $10–$25 for the GCIC criminal history report (varies by county, must be under 60 days old), the $175 exam fee, and the $170 license fee covering the first four years. Retakes cost the full $175 with no portion discount. A 25-hour post-license course is also required during the first year of licensure.
